thread.title: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s MacBook Air Unveiled 10 Years Ago, Today

author: Jim Breem
title: Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s MacBook Air Unveiled 10 Years Ago, Today
text:
January 15, 2018 Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s MacBook Air Unveiled 10 Years Ago, Today 
10 years ago today, Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) announced on January 15th, 2008, the original MacBook Air, that actually gave us a hint into the future plans and ambitions of Apple, which is aesthetically obsessed tech company, across all of their product lines. After a decade, now we’re taking a look at how the founder of MacBook Air actually set the pace for today’s modern devices, which is not only informing the direction of the iPhone and iPad but also redefining the Mac. After 10 years and seven generations later, Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s MacBook Air’s design hasn’t changed too much. 
The release of original MacBook Air more closely looked like a magician’s act than a product launch, as the “world’s thinnest notebook” has remained remarkably consistent, as there have been very less tweaks over the years, as we can see, like the second generation Magsafe connector, and a change to the ports, the wedge-shaped etc. 
Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s   $176.18   popped up 1.03% to reach at $177.09. Analyst’s mean target price for AAPL is $186.30   1.80. Stock value has moved between $118.06 – 177.09 in last one year. 
Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) yearly performance is 48.50% and net profit margin is 21.10%.   7.90%.  0.06%   49.81% ahead of its 52-week low. 
It’s important to consider the state of Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)’s Mac in early 2008. The MacBook was still housed in a plastic shell. The 15-inch MacBook Pro weighed a whopping 5.4 pounds. Only recently had the iMac gained an aluminum enclosure, and the Mac Pro was practically as tall and heavy as a living room end table. The MacBook Air felt like a radical departure from the familiar because it was. About Jim Breem
